svg.text: The two modes below each decode a 1024 × 1024 image from a 128 × 128 latent on four GPUs.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: They are alternatives, and both are priced in the same five columns.

svg.text: one decoder call, split into four bands of 32 latent rows

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Peak memory is rank-bound and every layer syncs, so the interconnect can be the bottleneck.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: There is nothing to choose here, since the band is the latent divided by the GPU count.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The image is what a single GPU would produce, apart from floating-point rounding.

svg.text: Convolutions swap edge rows, and norms reduce across all four ranks.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the same four GPUs, at two windows

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Peak memory is tile-bound and the decode needs only two collectives, but it repeats more work.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Window and overlap are yours to set in output pixels, so tune them to your VAE and your GPUs.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The two windows below are worked examples, chosen to show the trade rather than to be copied.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Full-width strips overlap less and stay contiguous in row-major memory, while a grid holds less at once.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The image is close but not exact: a blend hides seams, but norms over too small a tile can leave the colour blocky.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 344 px tall overlapping 88 px, full width

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Four strips, one per rank, have the same shape as the bands above, but they overlap and nothing syncs until the end.

svg.text: One call each, and one rank waits

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: With one strip per rank, there is nothing for the scheduler to decide.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The last strip is 32 latent rows where the others are 43.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: That shortfall is exactly the overlap, so closing it would thin the blend.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 432 × 296 px overlapping 72 px on both axes

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fifteen tiles across four ranks let the load be levelled, and a rank now holds a window rather than a strip.

svg.text: Each rank decodes its own, in turn

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Each rank starts with a contiguous run, then single tiles move to level it.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Rank 3 decodes five tiles to rank 0's three, and they still finish together.
